resource.name: ExplanationOfBenefit.identifier
resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.identifier
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: A unique identifier assigned to this explanation of benefit.
element.requirements: Allows EOBs to be distinguished and referenced.

resource.name: ExplanationOfBenefit.status
resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.status
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: The status of the resource instance.
element.comment: This element is labeled as a modifier because the status contains codes that mark the resource as not currently valid.
element.requirements: Need to track the status of the resource as 'draft' resources may undergo further edits while 'active' resources are immutable and may only have their status changed to 'cancelled'.
element.isModifierReason: This element is labeled as a modifier because it is a status element that contains status entered-in-error which means that the resource should not be treated as valid

binding.description: A code specifying the state of the resource instance.

resource.name: ExplanationOfBenefit.type
resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.type
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: The category of claim, e.g. oral, pharmacy, vision, institutional, professional.
element.comment: The majority of jurisdictions use: oral, pharmacy, vision, professional and institutional, or variants on those terms, as the general styles of claims. The valueset is extensible to accommodate other jurisdictional requirements.
element.requirements: Claim type determine the general sets of business rules applied for information requirements and adjudication.

binding.description: The type or discipline-style of the claim.

resource.name: ExplanationOfBenefit.subType
resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.subType
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: A finer grained suite of claim type codes which may convey additional information such as Inpatient vs Outpatient and/or a specialty service.
element.comment: This may contain the local bill type codes such as the US UB-04 bill type code.
element.requirements: Some jurisdictions need a finer grained claim type for routing and adjudication.

binding.description: A more granular claim typecode.

resource.name: ExplanationOfBenefit.use
resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.use
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: A code to indicate whether the nature of the request is: to request adjudication of products and services previously rendered; or requesting authorization and adjudication for provision in the future; or requesting the non-binding adjudication of the listed products and services which could be provided in the future.
element.requirements: This element is required to understand the nature of the request for adjudication.

binding.description: Complete, proposed, exploratory, other.

resource.name: ExplanationOfBenefit.patient
resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.patient
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: The recipient of the products and services
element.definition: The party to whom the professional services and/or products have been supplied or are being considered and for whom actual for forecast reimbursement is sought.
element.requirements: The patient must be supplied to the insurer so that confirmation of coverage and service history may be considered as part of the authorization and/or adjudiction.

resource.name: ExplanationOfBenefit.billablePeriod
resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.billablePeriod
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: Relevant time frame for the claim
element.definition: The period for which charges are being submitted.
element.comment: Typically this would be today or in the past for a claim, and today or in the future for preauthorizations and prodeterminations. Typically line item dates of service should fall within the billing period if one is specified.
element.requirements: A number jurisdictions required the submission of the billing period when submitting claims for example for hospital stays or long-term care.

resource.name: ExplanationOfBenefit.created
resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.created
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: The date this resource was created.
element.comment: This field is independent of the date of creation of the resource as it may reflect the creation date of a source document prior to digitization. Typically for claims all services must be completed as of this date.
element.requirements: Need to record a timestamp for use by both the recipient and the issuer.

resource.name: ExplanationOfBenefit.enterer
resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.enterer
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: Individual who created the claim, predetermination or preauthorization.
element.requirements: Some jurisdictions require the contact information for personnel completing claims.

resource.name: ExplanationOfBenefit.insurer
resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.insurer
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: The party responsible for authorization, adjudication and reimbursement.
element.requirements: To be a valid claim, preauthorization or predetermination there must be a party who is responsible for adjudicating the contents against a policy which provides benefits for the patient.

resource.name: ExplanationOfBenefit.provider
resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.provider
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: The provider which is responsible for the claim, predetermination or preauthorization.
element.comment: Typically this field would be 1..1 where this party is responsible for the claim but not necessarily professionally responsible for the provision of the individual products and services listed below.

resource.name: ExplanationOfBenefit.priority
resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.priority
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: The provider-required urgency of processing the request. Typical values include: stat, routine deferred.
element.comment: If a claim processor is unable to complete the processing as per the priority then they should generate and error and not process the request.
element.requirements: The provider may need to indicate their processing requirements so that the processor can indicate if they are unable to comply.

binding.description: The timeliness with which processing is required: stat, normal, deferred.

resource.name: ExplanationOfBenefit.fundsReserveRequested
resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.fundsReserveRequested
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: A code to indicate whether and for whom funds are to be reserved for future claims.
element.comment: This field is only used for preauthorizations.
element.requirements: In the case of a Pre-Determination/Pre-Authorization the provider may request that funds in the amount of the expected Benefit be reserved ('Patient' or 'Provider') to pay for the Benefits determined on the subsequent claim(s). 'None' explicitly indicates no funds reserving is requested.

binding.description: For whom funds are to be reserved: (Patient, Provider, None).

resource.name: ExplanationOfBenefit.fundsReserve
resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.fundsReserve
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: A code, used only on a response to a preauthorization, to indicate whether the benefits payable have been reserved and for whom.
element.comment: Fund would be release by a future claim quoting the preAuthRef of this response. Examples of values include: provider, patient, none.
element.requirements: Needed to advise the submitting provider on whether the rquest for reservation of funds has been honored.

binding.description: For whom funds are to be reserved: (Patient, Provider, None).

resource.name: ExplanationOfBenefit.related.claim
resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.related.claim
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: Reference to a related claim.
element.requirements: For workplace or other accidents it is common to relate separate claims arising from the same event.

resource.name: ExplanationOfBenefit.related.relationship
resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.related.relationship
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: How the reference claim is related
element.definition: A code to convey how the claims are related.
element.comment: For example, prior claim or umbrella.
element.requirements: Some insurers need a declaration of the type of relationship.

binding.description: Relationship of this claim to a related Claim.

resource.name: ExplanationOfBenefit.related.reference
resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.related.reference
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: An alternate organizational reference to the case or file to which this particular claim pertains.
element.comment: For example, Property/Casualty insurer claim number or Workers Compensation case number.
element.requirements: In cases where an event-triggered claim is being submitted to an insurer which requires a reference number to be specified on all exchanges.

resource.name: ExplanationOfBenefit.prescription
resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.prescription
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: Prescription to support the dispensing of pharmacy, device or vision products.
element.requirements: Required to authorize the dispensing of controlled substances and devices.

resource.name: ExplanationOfBenefit.originalPrescription
resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.originalPrescription
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: Original prescription if superceded by fulfiller
element.definition: Original prescription which has been superseded by this prescription to support the dispensing of pharmacy services, medications or products.
element.comment: For example, a physician may prescribe a medication which the pharmacy determines is contraindicated, or for which the patient has an intolerance, and therefor issues a new prescription for an alternate medication which has the same therapeutic intent. The prescription from the pharmacy becomes the 'prescription' and that from the physician becomes the 'original prescription'.
element.requirements: Often required when a fulfiller varies what is fulfilled from that authorized on the original prescription.

resource.name: ExplanationOfBenefit.payee.type
resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.payee.type
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: Type of Party to be reimbursed: Subscriber, provider, other.
element.requirements: Need to know who should receive payment with the most common situations being the Provider (assignment of benefits) or the Subscriber.

binding.description: A code for the party to be reimbursed.

resource.name: ExplanationOfBenefit.payee.party
resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.payee.party
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: Reference to the individual or organization to whom any payment will be made.
element.comment: Not required if the payee is 'subscriber' or 'provider'.
element.requirements: Need to provide demographics if the payee is not 'subscriber' nor 'provider'.

resource.name: ExplanationOfBenefit.referral
resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.referral
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: A reference to a referral resource.
element.comment: The referral resource which lists the date, practitioner, reason and other supporting information.
element.requirements: Some insurers require proof of referral to pay for services or to pay specialist rates for services.

resource.name: ExplanationOfBenefit.facility
resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.facility
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: Facility where the services were provided.
element.requirements: Insurance adjudication can be dependant on where services were delivered.

resource.name: ExplanationOfBenefit.claim
resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.claim
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: The business identifier for the instance of the adjudication request: claim predetermination or preauthorization.
element.requirements: To provide a link to the original adjudication request.

resource.name: ExplanationOfBenefit.claimResponse
resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.claimResponse
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: The business identifier for the instance of the adjudication response: claim, predetermination or preauthorization response.
element.requirements: To provide a link to the original adjudication response.

resource.name: ExplanationOfBenefit.outcome
resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.outcome
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: The outcome of the claim, predetermination, or preauthorization processing.
element.comment: The resource may be used to indicate that: the request has been held (queued) for processing; that it has been processed and errors found (error); that no errors were found and that some of the adjudication has been undertaken (partial) or that all of the adjudication has been undertaken (complete).
element.requirements: To advise the requestor of an overall processing outcome.

binding.description: The result of the claim processing.

resource.name: ExplanationOfBenefit.disposition
resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.disposition
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: A human readable description of the status of the adjudication.
element.requirements: Provided for user display.

resource.name: ExplanationOfBenefit.preAuthRef
resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.preAuthRef
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: Reference from the Insurer which is used in later communications which refers to this adjudication.
element.comment: This value is only present on preauthorization adjudications.
element.requirements: On subsequent claims, the insurer may require the provider to quote this value.

resource.name: ExplanationOfBenefit.preAuthRefPeriod
resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.preAuthRefPeriod
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: The timeframe during which the supplied preauthorization reference may be quoted on claims to obtain the adjudication as provided.
element.comment: This value is only present on preauthorization adjudications.
element.requirements: On subsequent claims, the insurer may require the provider to quote this value.

resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.careTeam.sequence
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: A number to uniquely identify care team entries.
element.requirements: Necessary to maintain the order of the care team and provide a mechanism to link individuals to claim details.

resource.name: ExplanationOfBenefit.careTeam.provider
resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.careTeam.provider
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: Member of the team who provided the product or service.
element.requirements: Often a regulatory requirement to specify the responsible provider.

resource.name: ExplanationOfBenefit.careTeam.responsible
resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.careTeam.responsible
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: The party who is billing and/or responsible for the claimed products or services.
element.comment: Responsible might not be required when there is only a single provider listed.
element.requirements: When multiple parties are present it is required to distinguish the lead or responsible individual.

resource.name: ExplanationOfBenefit.careTeam.role
resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.careTeam.role
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: The lead, assisting or supervising practitioner and their discipline if a multidisciplinary team.
element.comment: Role might not be required when there is only a single provider listed.
element.requirements: When multiple parties are present it is required to distinguish the roles performed by each member.

binding.description: The role codes for the care team members.

resource.name: ExplanationOfBenefit.careTeam.qualification
resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.careTeam.qualification
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: The qualification of the practitioner which is applicable for this service.
element.requirements: Need to specify which qualification a provider is delivering the product or service under.

binding.description: Provider professional qualifications.

element.requirements: Necessary to maintain the order of the supporting information items and provide a mechanism to link to claim details.

resource.name: ExplanationOfBenefit.supportingInfo.category
resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.supportingInfo.category
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: The general class of the information supplied: information; exception; accident, employment; onset, etc.
element.comment: This may contain a category for the local bill type codes.
element.requirements: Required to group or associate information items with common characteristics. For example: admission information or prior treatments.

element.short: Coverage to be used for adjudication
element.definition: A flag to indicate that this Coverage is to be used for adjudication of this claim when set to true.
element.comment: A patient may (will) have multiple insurance policies which provide reimbursement for healthcare services and products. For example, a person may also be covered by their spouse's policy and both appear in the list (and may be from the same insurer). This flag will be set to true for only one of the listed policies and that policy will be used for adjudicating this claim. Other claims would be created to request adjudication against the other listed policies.

element.requirements: Providers must quote previously issued authorization reference numbers in order to obtain adjudication as previously advised on the Preauthorization.

resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.item.adjudication.category
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: A code to indicate the information type of this adjudication record. Information types may include: the value submitted, maximum values or percentages allowed or payable under the plan, amounts that the patient is responsible for in-aggregate or pertaining to this item, amounts paid by other coverages, and the benefit payable for this item.
element.comment: For example, codes indicating: Co-Pay, deductible, eligible, benefit, tax, etc.
element.requirements: Needed to enable understanding of the context of the other information in the adjudication.

binding.description: The adjudication codes.

resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.item.adjudication.reason
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: A code supporting the understanding of the adjudication result and explaining variance from expected amount.
element.comment: For example, may indicate that the funds for this benefit type have been exhausted.
element.requirements: To support understanding of variance from adjudication expectations.

binding.description: Adjudication reason codes.

resource.name: ExplanationOfBenefit.item.adjudication.amount
resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.item.adjudication.amount
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: Monetary amount associated with the category.
element.comment: For example, amount submitted, eligible amount, co-payment, and benefit payable.
element.requirements: Most adjuciation categories convey a monetary amount.

resource.name: ExplanationOfBenefit.item.adjudication.value
resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.item.adjudication.value
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: A non-monetary value associated with the category. Mutually exclusive to the amount element above.
element.comment: For example: eligible percentage or co-payment percentage.
element.requirements: Some adjudication categories convey a percentage or a fixed value.

resource.name: ExplanationOfBenefit.item.detail.sequence
resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.item.detail.sequence
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: A claim detail line. Either a simple (a product or service) or a 'group' of sub-details which are simple items.
element.requirements: The items to be processed for adjudication.

resource.name: ExplanationOfBenefit.item.detail.revenue
resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.item.detail.revenue
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: The type of revenue or cost center providing the product and/or service.
element.requirements: Needed in the processing of institutional claims.

binding.description: Codes for the revenue or cost centers supplying the service and/or products.

resource.name: ExplanationOfBenefit.item.detail.category
resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.item.detail.category
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: Code to identify the general type of benefits under which products and services are provided.
element.comment: Examples include: Medical Care, Periodontics, Renal Dialysis, Vision Coverage.
element.requirements: Needed in the processing of institutional claims as this allows the insurer to determine whether a facial X-Ray is for dental, orthopedic, or facial surgery purposes.

binding.description: Benefit categories such as: oral, medical, vision, oral-basic etc.

resource.name: ExplanationOfBenefit.item.detail.productOrService
resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.item.detail.productOrService
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: Billing, service, product, or drug code
element.definition: When the value is a group code then this item collects a set of related claim details, otherwise this contains the product, service, drug or other billing code for the item.
element.comment: If this is an actual service or product line, i.e. not a Group, then use code to indicate the Professional Service or Product supplied (e.g. CTP, HCPCS, USCLS, ICD10, NCPDP, DIN, RxNorm, ACHI, CCI). If a grouping item then use a group code to indicate the type of thing being grouped e.g. 'glasses' or 'compound'.
element.requirements: Necessary to state what was provided or done.

binding.description: Allowable service and product codes.

resource.name: ExplanationOfBenefit.item.detail.modifier
resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.item.detail.modifier
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: Item typification or modifiers codes to convey additional context for the product or service.
element.comment: For example, in Oral whether the treatment is cosmetic or associated with TMJ, or for Medical whether the treatment was outside the clinic or out of office hours.
element.requirements: To support inclusion of the item for adjudication or to charge an elevated fee.

binding.description: Item type or modifiers codes, eg for Oral whether the treatment is cosmetic or associated with TMJ, or an appliance was lost or stolen.

resource.name: ExplanationOfBenefit.item.detail.programCode
resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.item.detail.programCode
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: Program the product or service is provided under
element.definition: Identifies the program under which this may be recovered.
element.comment: For example: Neonatal program, child dental program or drug users recovery program.
element.requirements: Commonly used in in the identification of publicly provided program focused on population segments or disease classifications.

binding.description: Program specific reason codes.

resource.name: ExplanationOfBenefit.item.detail.quantity
resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.item.detail.quantity
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: The number of repetitions of a service or product.
element.requirements: Required when the product or service code does not convey the quantity provided.

resource.name: ExplanationOfBenefit.item.detail.unitPrice
resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.item.detail.unitPrice
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: Fee, charge or cost per item
element.definition: If the item is not a group then this is the fee for the product or service, otherwise this is the total of the fees for the details of the group.
element.requirements: The amount charged to the patient by the provider for a single unit.

resource.name: ExplanationOfBenefit.item.detail.factor
resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.item.detail.factor
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: A real number that represents a multiplier used in determining the overall value of services delivered and/or goods received. The concept of a Factor allows for a discount or surcharge multiplier to be applied to a monetary amount.
element.comment: To show a 10% senior's discount, the value entered is: 0.90 (1.00 - 0.10).
element.requirements: When discounts are provided to a patient (example: Senior's discount) then this must be documented for adjudication.

resource.name: ExplanationOfBenefit.item.detail.net
resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.item.detail.net
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: The quantity times the unit price for an additional service or product or charge.
element.comment: For example, the formula: quantity * unitPrice * factor  = net. Quantity and factor are assumed to be 1 if not supplied.
element.requirements: Provides the total amount claimed  for the group (if a grouper) or the line item.

resource.name: ExplanationOfBenefit.item.detail.udi
resource.title: ExplanationOfBenefit.item.detail.udi
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: Unique Device Identifiers associated with this line item.
element.requirements: The UDI code allows the insurer to obtain device level information on the product supplied.

Resource definitions may define what content should be represented in the narrative to ensure clinical safety.

resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: The network service providing access (e.g., query, view, or retrieval) for the study. See implementation notes for information about using DICOM endpoints. A study-level endpoint applies to each series in the study, unless overridden by a series-level endpoint with the same Endpoint.connectionType.
element.comment: Typical endpoint types include DICOM WADO-RS, which is used to retrieve DICOM instances in native or rendered (e.g., JPG, PNG), formats using a RESTful API; DICOM WADO-URI, which can similarly retrieve native or rendered instances, except using an HTTP query-based approach; DICOM QIDO-RS, which allows RESTful query for DICOM information without retrieving the actual instances; or IHE Invoke Image Display (IID), which provides standard invocation of an imaging web viewer.
element.requirements: Access methods for viewing (e.g., IHE’s IID profile) or retrieving (e.g., DICOM’s WADO-URI and WADO-RS) the study or the study’s series or instances. The study-level baseLocation applies to each series in the study, unless overridden in series by a series-level baseLocation of the same type.

element.definition: Date vaccine administered or was to be administered.
element.comment: When immunizations are given a specific date and time should always be known.   When immunizations are patient reported, a specific date might not be known.  Although partial dates are allowed, an adult patient might not be able to recall the year a childhood immunization was given. An exact date is always preferable, but the use of the String data type is acceptable when an exact date is not known. A small number of vaccines (e.g. live oral typhoid vaccine) are given as a series of patient self-administered dose over a span of time. In cases like this, often, only the first dose (typically a provider supervised dose) is recorded with the occurrence indicating the date/time of the first dose.

resource.name: List.language

element.definition: The base language in which the resource is written.

If a language is specified, it should it also be specified on the div element in the html (see rules in HTML5 for information about the relationship between xml:lang and the html lang attribute).

binding.description: A human language.

resource.name: List.text
resource.title: List.text

element.short: Text summary of the resource, for human interpretation
element.definition: A human-readable narrative that contains a summary of the resource and can be used to represent the content of the resource to a human. The narrative need not encode all the structured data, but is required to contain sufficient detail to make it "clinically safe" for a human to just read the narrative. Resource definitions may define what content should be represented in the narrative to ensure clinical safety.
element.comment: Contained resources do not have narrative. Resources that are not contained SHOULD have a narrative. In some cases, a resource may only have text with little or no additional discrete data (as long as all minOccurs=1 elements are satisfied).  This may be necessary for data from legacy systems where information is captured as a "text blob" or where text is additionally entered raw or narrated and encoded information is added later.

binding.description: What the purpose of a list is.

resource.title: List.encounter

element.comment: The actual important date is the date of currency of the resources that were summarized, but it is usually assumed that these are current when the preparation occurs.
element.requirements: Identifies how current the list is which affects relevance.

resource.name: List.source
resource.title: List.source

element.definition: The entity responsible for deciding what the contents of the list were. Where the list was created by a human, this is the same as the author of the list.

element.isModifierReason: If deleted is true, then the item included in the list isn't actually part of the list anymore

element.short: A set of rules under which this content was created

element.comment: Asserting this rule set restricts the content to be only understood by a limited set of trading partners. This inherently limits the usefulness of the data in the long term. Wherever possible, implementers and/or specification writers should avoid using this element. Often, when used, the URL is a reference to an implementation guide that defines these special rules as part of it's narrative along with other profiles, value sets, etc.
element.isModifierReason: This element is labeled as a modifier because the implicit rules may provide additional knowledge about the resource that modifies it's meaning or interpretation

resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: The base language in which the resource is written.
element.comment: Language is provided to support indexing and accessibility (typically, services such as text to speech use the language tag). The html language tag in the narrative applies  to the narrative. The language tag on the resource may be used to specify the language of other presentations generated from the data in the resource. Not all the content has to be in the base language. The Resource.language should not be assumed to apply to the narrative automatically. If a language is specified, it should it also be specified on the div element in the html (see rules in HTML5 for information about the relationship between xml:lang and the html lang attribute).

binding.description: A human language.

resource.name: Measure.text

element.definition: A human-readable narrative that contains a summary of the resource and can be used to represent the content of the resource to a human. The narrative need not encode all the structured data, but is required to contain sufficient detail to make it "clinically safe" for a human to just read the narrative. Resource definitions may define what content should be represented in the narrative to ensure clinical safety.
element.comment: Contained resources do not have narrative. Resources that are not contained SHOULD have a narrative. In some cases, a resource may only have text with little or no additional discrete data (as long as all minOccurs=1 elements are satisfied).  This may be necessary for data from legacy systems where information is captured as a "text blob" or where text is additionally entered raw or narrated and encoded information is added later.

resource.name: Measure.url
resource.title: Measure.url
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: Canonical identifier for this measure, represented as a URI (globally unique)
element.definition: An absolute URI that is used to identify this measure when it is referenced in a specification, model, design or an instance; also called its canonical identifier. This SHOULD be globally unique and SHOULD be a literal address at which at which an authoritative instance of this measure is (or will be) published. This URL can be the target of a canonical reference. It SHALL remain the same when the measure is stored on different servers.
element.comment:
Can be a urn:uuid: or a urn:oid: but real http: addresses are preferred.  Multiple instances may share the same URL if they have a distinct version.

The determination of when to create a new version of a resource (same url, new version) vs. defining a new artifact is up to the author.  Considerations for making this decision are found in [Technical and Business Versions](resource.html#versions). 

In some cases, the resource can no longer be found at the stated url, but the url itself cannot change. Implementations can use the [meta.source](resource.html#meta) element to indicate where the current master source of the resource can be found.
element.requirements: Allows the measure to be referenced by a single globally unique identifier.

resource.name: Measure.identifier
resource.title: Measure.identifier
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: A formal identifier that is used to identify this measure when it is represented in other formats, or referenced in a specification, model, design or an instance.
element.comment: Typically, this is used for identifiers that can go in an HL7 V3 II (instance identifier) data type, and can then identify this measure outside of FHIR, where it is not possible to use the logical URI.
element.requirements: Allows externally provided and/or usable business identifiers to be easily associated with the module.

resource.name: Measure.version
resource.title: Measure.version
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: The identifier that is used to identify this version of the measure when it is referenced in a specification, model, design or instance. This is an arbitrary value managed by the measure author and is not expected to be globally unique. For example, it might be a timestamp (e.g. yyyymmdd) if a managed version is not available. There is also no expectation that versions can be placed in a lexicographical sequence. To provide a version consistent with the Decision Support Service specification, use the format Major.Minor.Revision (e.g. 1.0.0). For more information on versioning knowledge assets, refer to the Decision Support Service specification. Note that a version is required for non-experimental active artifacts.
element.comment: There may be different measure instances that have the same identifier but different versions.  The version can be appended to the url in a reference to allow a reference to a particular business version of the measure with the format [url]|[version].

resource.name: Measure.name
resource.title: Measure.name
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: A natural language name identifying the measure. This name should be usable as an identifier for the module by machine processing applications such as code generation.
element.comment: The name is not expected to be globally unique. The name should be a simple alphanumeric type name to ensure that it is machine-processing friendly.
element.requirements: Support human navigation and code generation.

resource.name: Measure.title
resource.title: Measure.title
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: A short, descriptive, user-friendly title for the measure.
element.comment: This name does not need to be machine-processing friendly and may contain punctuation, white-space, etc.

resource.name: Measure.subtitle
resource.title: Measure.subtitle
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: An explanatory or alternate title for the measure giving additional information about its content.

resource.name: Measure.status
resource.title: Measure.status
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: The status of this measure. Enables tracking the life-cycle of the content.
element.comment: Allows filtering of measures that are appropriate for use versus not.
element.isModifierReason: This is labeled as "Is Modifier" because applications should not use a retired {{title}} without due consideration

binding.description: The lifecycle status of an artifact.

resource.name: Measure.experimental
resource.title: Measure.experimental
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: For testing purposes, not real usage
element.definition: A Boolean value to indicate that this measure is authored for testing purposes (or education/evaluation/marketing) and is not intended to be used for genuine usage.
element.comment: Allows filtering of measures that are appropriate for use versus not.
element.requirements: Enables experimental content to be developed following the same lifecycle that would be used for a production-level measure.

resource.name: Measure.subject[x]
resource.title: Measure.subject[x]
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: E.g. Patient, Practitioner, RelatedPerson, Organization, Location, Device
element.definition: The intended subjects for the measure. If this element is not provided, a Patient subject is assumed, but the subject of the measure can be anything.
element.comment: The subject of the measure is critical in interpreting the criteria definitions, as the logic in the measures is evaluated with respect to a particular subject. This corresponds roughly to the notion of a Compartment in that it limits what content is available based on its relationship to the subject. In CQL, this corresponds to the context declaration.
element.meaningWhenMissing: Patient

binding.description: The possible types of subjects for a measure (E.g. Patient, Practitioner, Organization, Location, etc.).

resource.name: Measure.date
resource.title: Measure.date
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: The date  (and optionally time) when the measure was published. The date must change when the business version changes and it must change if the status code changes. In addition, it should change when the substantive content of the measure changes.
element.comment: Note that this is not the same as the resource last-modified-date, since the resource may be a secondary representation of the measure. Additional specific dates may be added as extensions or be found by consulting Provenances associated with past versions of the resource.

resource.name: Measure.publisher
resource.title: Measure.publisher
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: Name of the publisher (organization or individual)
element.definition: The name of the organization or individual that published the measure.
element.comment: Usually an organization but may be an individual. The publisher (or steward) of the measure is the organization or individual primarily responsible for the maintenance and upkeep of the measure. This is not necessarily the same individual or organization that developed and initially authored the content. The publisher is the primary point of contact for questions or issues with the measure. This item SHOULD be populated unless the information is available from context.
element.requirements: Helps establish the "authority/credibility" of the measure.  May also allow for contact.

resource.name: Measure.contact
resource.title: Measure.contact
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: Contact details to assist a user in finding and communicating with the publisher.
element.comment: May be a web site, an email address, a telephone number, etc.

resource.name: Measure.description
resource.title: Measure.description
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: Natural language description of the measure
element.definition: A free text natural language description of the measure from a consumer's perspective.
element.comment: This description can be used to capture details such as why the measure was built, comments about misuse, instructions for clinical use and interpretation, literature references, examples from the paper world, etc. It is not a rendering of the measure as conveyed in the 'text' field of the resource itself. This item SHOULD be populated unless the information is available from context (e.g. the language of the measure is presumed to be the predominant language in the place the measure was created).

resource.name: Measure.useContext
resource.title: Measure.useContext
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: The context that the content is intended to support
element.definition: The content was developed with a focus and intent of supporting the contexts that are listed. These contexts may be general categories (gender, age, ...) or may be references to specific programs (insurance plans, studies, ...) and may be used to assist with indexing and searching for appropriate measure instances.
element.comment: When multiple useContexts are specified, there is no expectation that all or any of the contexts apply.
element.requirements: Assist in searching for appropriate content.

resource.name: Measure.jurisdiction
resource.title: Measure.jurisdiction
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: A legal or geographic region in which the measure is intended to be used.
element.comment: It may be possible for the measure to be used in jurisdictions other than those for which it was originally designed or intended.

binding.description: Countries and regions within which this artifact is targeted for use.

resource.name: Measure.purpose
resource.title: Measure.purpose
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: Explanation of why this measure is needed and why it has been designed as it has.
element.comment: This element does not describe the usage of the measure. Instead, it provides traceability of ''why'' the resource is either needed or ''why'' it is defined as it is.  This may be used to point to source materials or specifications that drove the structure of this measure.

resource.name: Measure.usage
resource.title: Measure.usage
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: Describes the clinical usage of the measure
element.definition: A detailed description, from a clinical perspective, of how the measure is used.

resource.name: Measure.copyright
resource.title: Measure.copyright
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: A copyright statement relating to the measure and/or its contents. Copyright statements are generally legal restrictions on the use and publishing of the measure.
element.requirements: Consumers must be able to determine any legal restrictions on the use of the measure and/or its content.

resource.name: Measure.approvalDate
resource.title: Measure.approvalDate
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: When the measure was approved by publisher
element.definition: The date on which the resource content was approved by the publisher. Approval happens once when the content is officially approved for usage.
element.comment: The 'date' element may be more recent than the approval date because of minor changes or editorial corrections.

resource.name: Measure.lastReviewDate
resource.title: Measure.lastReviewDate
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: When the measure was last reviewed
element.definition: The date on which the resource content was last reviewed. Review happens periodically after approval but does not change the original approval date.
element.comment: If specified, this date follows the original approval date.
element.requirements: Gives a sense of how "current" the content is.  Resources that have not been reviewed in a long time may have a risk of being less appropriate/relevant.

resource.name: Measure.effectivePeriod
resource.title: Measure.effectivePeriod
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: When the measure is expected to be used
element.definition: The period during which the measure content was or is planned to be in active use.
element.comment: The effective period for a measure  determines when the content is applicable for usage and is independent of publication and review dates. For example, a measure intended to be used for the year 2016 might be published in 2015.
element.requirements: Allows establishing a transition before a resource comes into effect and also allows for a sunsetting  process when new versions of the measure are or are expected to be used instead.

resource.name: Measure.topic
resource.title: Measure.topic
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: The category of the measure, such as Education, Treatment, Assessment, etc.
element.definition: Descriptive topics related to the content of the measure. Topics provide a high-level categorization grouping types of measures that can be useful for filtering and searching.
element.requirements: Repositories must be able to determine how to categorize the measure so that it can be found by topical searches.

binding.description: High-level categorization of the definition, used for searching, sorting, and filtering.

resource.name: Measure.author
resource.title: Measure.author

element.definition: An individiual or organization primarily involved in the creation and maintenance of the content.

resource.name: Measure.editor
resource.title: Measure.editor
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: An individual or organization primarily responsible for internal coherence of the content.

resource.name: Measure.reviewer
resource.title: Measure.reviewer
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: An individual or organization primarily responsible for review of some aspect of the content.

resource.name: Measure.endorser
resource.title: Measure.endorser

mapping.map: .participation[typeCode=VRF] {not clear whether VRF best corresponds to reviewer or endorser}

resource.name: Measure.relatedArtifact
resource.title: Measure.relatedArtifact
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: Related artifacts such as additional documentation, justification, or bibliographic references.
element.comment: Each related artifact is either an attachment, or a reference to another resource, but not both.
element.requirements: Measures must be able to provide enough information for consumers of the content (and/or interventions or results produced by the content) to be able to determine and understand the justification for and evidence in support of the content.

resource.name: Measure.library
resource.title: Measure.library
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: A reference to a Library resource containing the formal logic used by the measure.

resource.name: Measure.disclaimer
resource.title: Measure.disclaimer
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: Disclaimer for use of the measure or its referenced content
element.definition: Notices and disclaimers regarding the use of the measure or related to intellectual property (such as code systems) referenced by the measure.
element.requirements: Some organizations require that notices and disclosures be included when publishing measures that reference their intellecutal property.

resource.name: Measure.scoring
resource.title: Measure.scoring
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: Indicates how the calculation is performed for the measure, including proportion, ratio, continuous-variable, and cohort. The value set is extensible, allowing additional measure scoring types to be represented.

binding.description: The scoring type of the measure.

resource.name: Measure.compositeScoring
resource.title: Measure.compositeScoring
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: If this is a composite measure, the scoring method used to combine the component measures to determine the composite score.

binding.description: The composite scoring method of the measure.

resource.name: Measure.type
resource.title: Measure.type
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: Indicates whether the measure is used to examine a process, an outcome over time, a patient-reported outcome, or a structure measure such as utilization.

binding.description: The type of measure (includes codes from 2.16.840.1.113883.1.11.20368).

resource.name: Measure.riskAdjustment
resource.title: Measure.riskAdjustment
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: How risk adjustment is applied for this measure
element.definition: A description of the risk adjustment factors that may impact the resulting score for the measure and how they may be accounted for when computing and reporting measure results.
element.comment: Describes the method of adjusting for clinical severity and conditions present at the start of care that can influence patient outcomes for making valid comparisons of outcome measures across providers. Indicates whether a measure is subject to the statistical process for reducing, removing, or clarifying the influences of confounding factors to allow for more useful comparisons.

resource.name: Measure.rateAggregation
resource.title: Measure.rateAggregation
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: How is rate aggregation performed for this measure
element.definition: Describes how to combine the information calculated, based on logic in each of several populations, into one summarized result.
element.comment: The measure rate for an organization or clinician is based upon the entities’ aggregate data and summarizes the performance of the entity over a given time period (e.g., monthly, quarterly, yearly). The aggregated data are derived from the results of a specific measure algorithm and, if appropriate, the application of specific risk adjustment models.  Can also be used to describe how to risk adjust the data based on supplemental data elements described in the eMeasure (e.g., pneumonia hospital measures antibiotic selection in the ICU versus non-ICU and then the roll-up of the two). This could be applied to aggregated cohort measure definitions (e.g., CDC's aggregate reporting for TB at the state level).

resource.name: Measure.rationale
resource.title: Measure.rationale
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: Detailed description of why the measure exists
element.definition: Provides a succinct statement of the need for the measure. Usually includes statements pertaining to importance criterion: impact, gap in care, and evidence.
element.requirements: Measure developers need to be able to provide a detailed description of the purpose of the measure. This element provides detailed rationale, where the purpose element provides a summary of the rationale.

resource.name: Measure.clinicalRecommendationStatement
resource.title: Measure.clinicalRecommendationStatement
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: Provides a summary of relevant clinical guidelines or other clinical recommendations supporting the measure.

resource.name: Measure.improvementNotation
resource.title: Measure.improvementNotation
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: Information on whether an increase or decrease in score is the preferred result (e.g., a higher score indicates better quality OR a lower score indicates better quality OR quality is within a range).
element.requirements: Measure consumers and implementers must be able to determine how to interpret a measure score.

binding.description: Observation values that indicate what change in a measurement value or score is indicative of an improvement in the measured item or scored issue.

resource.name: Measure.definition
resource.title: Measure.definition
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: Defined terms used in the measure documentation
element.definition: Provides a description of an individual term used within the measure.
element.requirements: Measure developers must be able to provide precise definitions of terms used within measure descriptions and guidance to help communicate the intent of the measure.

resource.name: Measure.guidance
resource.title: Measure.guidance
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: Additional guidance for the measure including how it can be used in a clinical context, and the intent of the measure.
element.requirements: Measure developers must be able to provide additional guidance for implementers to understand the intent with greater specificity than that provided in the population criteria of the measure. This element provides detailed guidance, where the usage element provides a summary of the guidance.

resource.name: Measure.group.id
resource.title: Measure.group.id
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: Unique id for the element within a resource (for internal references). This may be any string value that does not contain spaces.

element.short: A set of rules under which this content was created
element.definition: A reference to a set of rules that were followed when the resource was constructed, and which must be understood when processing the content. Often, this is a reference to an implementation guide that defines the special rules along with other profiles etc.
element.comment: Asserting this rule set restricts the content to be only understood by a limited set of trading partners. This inherently limits the usefulness of the data in the long term. However, the existing health eco-system is highly fractured, and not yet ready to define, collect, and exchange data in a generally computable sense. Wherever possible, implementers and/or specification writers should avoid using this element. Often, when used, the URL is a reference to an implementation guide that defines these special rules as part of it's narrative along with other profiles, value sets, etc.
element.isModifierReason: This element is labeled as a modifier because the implicit rules may provide additional knowledge about the resource that modifies it's meaning or interpretation

resource.title: Media.language

element.definition: The base language in which the resource is written.
element.comment: Language is provided to support indexing and accessibility (typically, services such as text to speech use the language tag). The html language tag in the narrative applies  to the narrative. The language tag on the resource may be used to specify the language of other presentations generated from the data in the resource. Not all the content has to be in the base language. The Resource.language should not be assumed to apply to the narrative automatically. If a language is specified, it should it also be specified on the div element in the html (see rules in HTML5 for information about the relationship between xml:lang and the html lang attribute).

binding.description: A human language.

resource.name: Media.text
resource.title: Media.text
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: Text summary of the resource, for human interpretation
element.definition: A human-readable narrative that contains a summary of the resource and can be used to represent the content of the resource to a human. The narrative need not encode all the structured data, but is required to contain sufficient detail to make it "clinically safe" for a human to just read the narrative. Resource definitions may define what content should be represented in the narrative to ensure clinical safety.
element.comment: Contained resources do not have narrative. Resources that are not contained SHOULD have a narrative. In some cases, a resource may only have text with little or no additional discrete data (as long as all minOccurs=1 elements are satisfied).  This may be necessary for data from legacy systems where information is captured as a "text blob" or where text is additionally entered raw or narrated and encoded information is added later.

element.comment: This should never be done when the content can be identified properly, as once identification is lost, it is extremely difficult (and context dependent) to restore it again. Contained resources may have profiles and tags In their meta elements, but SHALL NOT have security labels.

resource.name: MedicationKnowledge.status
resource.title: MedicationKnowledge.status
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: A code to indicate if the medication is in active use.  The status refers to the validity about the information of the medication and not to its medicinal properties.
element.comment: This status is intended to identify if the medication in a local system is in active use within a drug database or inventory.  For example, a pharmacy system may create a new drug file record for a compounded product "ABC Hospital Special Cream" with an active status.  At some point in the future, it may be determined that the drug record was created with an error and the status is changed to "entered in error".   This status is not intended to specify if a medication is part of a particular formulary.  It is possible that the drug record may be referenced by multiple formularies or catalogues and each of those entries would have a separate status.
element.isModifierReason: This element changes the interpretation of all descriptive attributes.

binding.description: A coded concept defining if the medication is in active use.

element.definition: The date  (and optionally time) when the message definition was published. The date must change when the business version changes and it must change if the status code changes. In addition, it should change when the substantive content of the message definition changes.
element.comment: Note that this is not the same as the resource last-modified-date, since the resource may be a secondary representation of the message definition. resource.name: MessageDefinition.publisher
resource.title: MessageDefinition.publisher

element.short: Name of the publisher (organization or individual)
element.definition: The name of the organization or individual that published the message definition.
element.comment: Usually an organization but may be an individual. The publisher (or steward) of the message definition is the organization or individual primarily responsible for the maintenance and upkeep of the message definition. This is not necessarily the same individual or organization that developed and initially authored the content. The publisher is the primary point of contact for questions or issues with the message definition. This item SHOULD be populated unless the information is available from context.
element.requirements: Helps establish the "authority/credibility" of the message definition.  May also allow for contact.

resource.name: MessageDefinition.contact
resource.title: MessageDefinition.contact

resource.name: MessageDefinition.description
resource.title: MessageDefinition.description

element.definition: A free text natural language description of the message definition from a consumer's perspective.
element.comment: This description can be used to capture details such as why the message definition was built, comments about misuse, instructions for clinical use and interpretation, literature references, examples from the paper world, etc. It is not a rendering of the message definition as conveyed in the 'text' field of the resource itself. This item SHOULD be populated unless the information is available from context (e.g. the language of the message definition is presumed to be the predominant language in the place the message definition was created).

Not all the content has to be in the base language. The Resource.language should not be assumed to apply to the narrative automatically. If a language is specified, it should it also be specified on the div element in the html (see rules in HTML5 for information about the relationship between xml:lang and the html lang attribute).

Resource definitions may define what content should be represented in the narrative to ensure clinical safety.
element.comment: Contained resources do not have narrative. Resources that are not contained SHOULD have a narrative. In some cases, a resource may only have text with little or no additional discrete data (as long as all minOccurs=1 elements are satisfied).  This may be necessary for data from legacy systems where information is captured as a "text blob" or where text is additionally entered raw or narrated and encoded information is added later.

resource.name: MolecularSequence.quality.truthTP
resource.title: MolecularSequence.quality.truthTP
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: True positives from the perspective of the truth data
element.definition: True positives, from the perspective of the truth data, i.e. the number of sites in the Truth Call Set for which there are paths through the Query Call Set that are consistent with all of the alleles at this site, and for which there is an accurate genotype call for the event.

resource.name: MolecularSequence.quality.queryTP
resource.title: MolecularSequence.quality.queryTP
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: True positives from the perspective of the query data
element.definition: True positives, from the perspective of the query data, i.e. the number of sites in the Query Call Set for which there are paths through the Truth Call Set that are consistent with all of the alleles at this site, and for which there is an accurate genotype call for the event.

resource.name: MolecularSequence.quality.truthFN
resource.title: MolecularSequence.quality.truthFN
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: False negatives, i.e. the number of sites in the Truth Call Set for which there is no path through the Query Call Set that is consistent with all of the alleles at this site, or sites for which there is an inaccurate genotype call for the event. Sites with correct variant but incorrect genotype are counted here.

resource.name: MolecularSequence.quality.queryFP
resource.title: MolecularSequence.quality.queryFP
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: False positives, i.e. the number of sites in the Query Call Set for which there is no path through the Truth Call Set that is consistent with this site. Sites with correct variant but incorrect genotype are counted here.

resource.name: MolecularSequence.quality.gtFP
resource.title: MolecularSequence.quality.gtFP
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: False positives where the non-REF alleles in the Truth and Query Call Sets match
element.definition: The number of false positives where the non-REF alleles in the Truth and Query Call Sets match (i.e. cases where the truth is 1/1 and the query is 0/1 or similar).

resource.name: MolecularSequence.quality.precision
resource.title: MolecularSequence.quality.precision

resource.name: MolecularSequence.quality.recall
resource.title: MolecularSequence.quality.recall

resource.title: MolecularSequence.quality.fScore

element.definition: Harmonic mean of Recall and Precision, computed as: 2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall).

The focus of an observation could also be an existing condition,  an intervention, the subject's diet,  another observation of the subject,  or a body structure such as tumor or implanted device.   An example use case would be using the Observation resource to capture whether the mother is trained to change her child's tracheostomy tube. In this example, the child is the patient of record and the mother is the focus.
element.comment: Typically, an observation is made about the subject - a patient, or group of patients, location, or device - and the distinction between the subject and what is directly measured for an observation is specified in the observation code itself ( e.g., "Blood Glucose") and does not need to be represented separately using this element.  Use `specimen` if a reference to a specimen is required.  If a code is required instead of a resource use either  `bodysite` for bodysites or the standard extension [focusCode](extension-observation-focuscode.html).

resource.name: Observation.encounter

resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: Healthcare event during which this observation is made

element.comment: This will typically be the encounter the event occurred within, but some events may be initiated prior to or after the official completion of an encounter but still be tied to the context of the encounter (e.g. pre-admission laboratory tests).
element.requirements: For some observations it may be important to know the link between an observation and a particular encounter.

resource.name: Observation.effective[x]

element.definition: The time or time-period the observed value is asserted as being true. For biological subjects - e.g. human patients - this is usually called the "physiologically relevant time". This is usually either the time of the procedure or of specimen collection, but very often the source of the date/time is not known, only the date/time itself.
element.comment: At least a date should be present unless this observation is a historical report.  For recording imprecise or "fuzzy" times (For example, a blood glucose measurement taken "after breakfast") use the [Timing](datatypes.html#timing) datatype which allow the measurement to be tied to regular life events.
element.requirements: Knowing when an observation was deemed true is important to its relevance as well as determining trends.

element.definition: Provides a reason why the expected value in the element Observation.value[x] is missing.
element.comment:
Null or exceptional values can be represented two ways in FHIR Observations.  One way is to simply include them in the value set and represent the exceptions in the value.  For example, measurement values for a serology test could be  "detected", "not detected", "inconclusive", or  "specimen unsatisfactory".   

The alternate way is to use the value element for actual observations and use the explicit dataAbsentReason element to record exceptional values.  For example, the dataAbsentReason code "error" could be used when the measurement was not completed. Note that an observation may only be reported if there are values to report. For example differential cell counts values may be reported only when > 0.  Because of these options, use-case agreements are required to interpret general observations for null or exceptional values.

element.definition:
Whether this patient record is in active use. 
Many systems use this property to mark as non-current patients, such as those that have not been seen for a period of time based on an organization's business rules.

It is often used to filter patient lists to exclude inactive patients

Deceased patients may also be marked as inactive for the same reasons, but may be active for some time after death.

element.comment: The gender might not match the biological sex as determined by genetics or the individual's preferred identification. Note that for both humans and particularly animals, there are other legitimate possibilities than male and female, though the vast majority of systems and contexts only support male and female.  Systems providing decision support or enforcing business rules should ideally do this on the basis of Observations dealing with the specific sex or gender aspect of interest (anatomical, chromosomal, social, etc.)  However, because these observations are infrequently recorded, defaulting to the administrative gender is common practice.  Where such defaulting occurs, rule enforcement should allow for the variation between administrative and biological, chromosomal and other gender aspects.  For example, an alert about a hysterectomy on a male should be handled as a warning or overridable error, not a "hard" error.  See the Patient Gender and Sex section for additional information about communicating patient gender and sex.

resource.title: Patient.generalPractitioner
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: Patient's nominated care provider.
element.comment:
This may be the primary care provider (in a GP context), or it may be a patient nominated care manager in a community/disability setting, or even organization that will provide people to perform the care provider roles.  It is not to be used to record Care Teams, these should be in a CareTeam resource that may be linked to the CarePlan or EpisodeOfCare resources.
Multiple GPs may be recorded against the patient for various reasons, such as a student that has his home GP listed along with the GP at university during the school semesters, or a "fly-in/fly-out" worker that has the onsite GP also included with his home GP to remain aware of medical issues.

Jurisdictions may decide that they can profile this down to 1 if desired, or 1 per type.

element.short: A set of rules under which this content was created
element.definition: A reference to a set of rules that were followed when the resource was constructed, and which must be understood when processing the content. Often, this is a reference to an implementation guide that defines the special rules along with other profiles etc.
element.comment: Asserting this rule set restricts the content to be only understood by a limited set of trading partners. This inherently limits the usefulness of the data in the long term. However, the existing health eco-system is highly fractured, and not yet ready to define, collect, and exchange data in a generally computable sense. Wherever possible, implementers and/or specification writers should avoid using this element. Often, when used, the URL is a reference to an implementation guide that defines these special rules as part of it's narrative along with other profiles, value sets, etc.
element.isModifierReason: This element is labeled as a modifier because the implicit rules may provide additional knowledge about the resource that modifies it's meaning or interpretation

resource.title: Questionnaire.language
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: The base language in which the resource is written.
element.comment: Language is provided to support indexing and accessibility (typically, services such as text to speech use the language tag). The html language tag in the narrative applies  to the narrative. The language tag on the resource may be used to specify the language of other presentations generated from the data in the resource. Not all the content has to be in the base language. The Resource.language should not be assumed to apply to the narrative automatically. If a language is specified, it should it also be specified on the div element in the html (see rules in HTML5 for information about the relationship between xml:lang and the html lang attribute).

binding.description: A human language.

resource.name: Questionnaire.text
resource.title: Questionnaire.text
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: Text summary of the resource, for human interpretation
element.definition: A human-readable narrative that contains a summary of the resource and can be used to represent the content of the resource to a human. The narrative need not encode all the structured data, but is required to contain sufficient detail to make it "clinically safe" for a human to just read the narrative. Resource definitions may define what content should be represented in the narrative to ensure clinical safety.
element.comment: Contained resources do not have narrative. Resources that are not contained SHOULD have a narrative. In some cases, a resource may only have text with little or no additional discrete data (as long as all minOccurs=1 elements are satisfied).  This may be necessary for data from legacy systems where information is captured as a "text blob" or where text is additionally entered raw or narrated and encoded information is added later.
