element.comment: This should never be done when the content can be identified properly, as once identification is lost, it is extremely difficult (and context dependent) to restore it again. Contained resources may have profiles and tags In their meta elements, but SHALL NOT have security labels.

resource.name: Questionnaire.url
resource.title: Questionnaire.url
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: Canonical identifier for this questionnaire, represented as a URI (globally unique)
element.definition: An absolute URI that is used to identify this questionnaire when it is referenced in a specification, model, design or an instance; also called its canonical identifier. This SHOULD be globally unique and SHOULD be a literal address at which at which an authoritative instance of this questionnaire is (or will be) published. This URL can be the target of a canonical reference. It SHALL remain the same when the questionnaire is stored on different servers.
element.comment: The name of the referenced questionnaire can be conveyed using the http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/display extension.
element.requirements: …  This is the id that will be used to link a QuestionnaireResponse to the Questionnaire the response is for.

resource.name: Questionnaire.identifier
resource.title: Questionnaire.identifier
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: A formal identifier that is used to identify this questionnaire when it is represented in other formats, or referenced in a specification, model, design or an instance.
element.comment: Typically, this is used for identifiers that can go in an HL7 V3 II (instance identifier) data type, and can then identify this questionnaire outside of FHIR, where it is not possible to use the logical URI.
element.requirements: Allows externally provided and/or usable business identifiers to be easily associated with the module.

resource.name: Questionnaire.version
resource.title: Questionnaire.version
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: The identifier that is used to identify this version of the questionnaire when it is referenced in a specification, model, design or instance. This is an arbitrary value managed by the questionnaire author and is not expected to be globally unique. For example, it might be a timestamp (e.g. yyyymmdd) if a managed version is not available. There is also no expectation that versions can be placed in a lexicographical sequence.
element.comment: There may be different questionnaire instances that have the same identifier but different versions.  The version can be appended to the url in a reference to allow a reference to a particular business version of the questionnaire with the format [url]|[version].

resource.name: Questionnaire.name
resource.title: Questionnaire.name
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: A natural language name identifying the questionnaire. This name should be usable as an identifier for the module by machine processing applications such as code generation.
element.comment: The name is not expected to be globally unique. The name should be a simple alphanumeric type name to ensure that it is machine-processing friendly.
element.requirements: Support human navigation and code generation.

resource.name: Questionnaire.title
resource.title: Questionnaire.title
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: A short, descriptive, user-friendly title for the questionnaire.
element.comment: This name does not need to be machine-processing friendly and may contain punctuation, white-space, etc.

resource.name: Questionnaire.derivedFrom
resource.title: Questionnaire.derivedFrom
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: The URL of a Questionnaire that this Questionnaire is based on.
element.requirements: Allows a Questionnaire to be created based on another Questionnaire.

resource.name: Questionnaire.status
resource.title: Questionnaire.status
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: The status of this questionnaire. Enables tracking the life-cycle of the content.
element.comment: Allows filtering of questionnaires that are appropriate for use versus not.
element.isModifierReason: This is labeled as "Is Modifier" because applications should not use a retired {{title}} without due consideration

binding.description: The lifecycle status of an artifact.

resource.name: Questionnaire.experimental
resource.title: Questionnaire.experimental
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: For testing purposes, not real usage
element.definition: A Boolean value to indicate that this questionnaire is authored for testing purposes (or education/evaluation/marketing) and is not intended to be used for genuine usage.
element.comment: Allows filtering of questionnaires that are appropriate for use versus not.
element.requirements: Enables experimental content to be developed following the same lifecycle that would be used for a production-level questionnaire.

resource.name: Questionnaire.subjectType
resource.title: Questionnaire.subjectType
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: Resource that can be subject of QuestionnaireResponse
element.definition: The types of subjects that can be the subject of responses created for the questionnaire.
element.comment: If none are specified, then the subject is unlimited.

binding.description: One of the resource types defined as part of this version of FHIR.

resource.name: Questionnaire.date
resource.title: Questionnaire.date
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: The date  (and optionally time) when the questionnaire was published. The date must change when the business version changes and it must change if the status code changes. In addition, it should change when the substantive content of the questionnaire changes.
element.comment: Note that this is not the same as the resource last-modified-date, since the resource may be a secondary representation of the questionnaire. Additional specific dates may be added as extensions or be found by consulting Provenances associated with past versions of the resource.

resource.name: Questionnaire.publisher
resource.title: Questionnaire.publisher
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: Name of the publisher (organization or individual)
element.definition: The name of the organization or individual that published the questionnaire.
element.comment: Usually an organization but may be an individual. The publisher (or steward) of the questionnaire is the organization or individual primarily responsible for the maintenance and upkeep of the questionnaire. This is not necessarily the same individual or organization that developed and initially authored the content. The publisher is the primary point of contact for questions or issues with the questionnaire. This item SHOULD be populated unless the information is available from context.
element.requirements: Helps establish the "authority/credibility" of the questionnaire.  May also allow for contact.

resource.name: Questionnaire.contact
resource.title: Questionnaire.contact
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: Contact details to assist a user in finding and communicating with the publisher.
element.comment: May be a web site, an email address, a telephone number, etc.

resource.name: Questionnaire.description
resource.title: Questionnaire.description
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: Natural language description of the questionnaire
element.definition: A free text natural language description of the questionnaire from a consumer's perspective.
element.comment: This description can be used to capture details such as why the questionnaire was built, comments about misuse, instructions for clinical use and interpretation, literature references, examples from the paper world, etc. It is not a rendering of the questionnaire as conveyed in the 'text' field of the resource itself. This item SHOULD be populated unless the information is available from context (e.g. the language of the questionnaire is presumed to be the predominant language in the place the questionnaire was created).

resource.name: Questionnaire.useContext
resource.title: Questionnaire.useContext
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: The context that the content is intended to support
element.definition: The content was developed with a focus and intent of supporting the contexts that are listed. These contexts may be general categories (gender, age, ...) or may be references to specific programs (insurance plans, studies, ...) and may be used to assist with indexing and searching for appropriate questionnaire instances.
element.comment: When multiple useContexts are specified, there is no expectation that all or any of the contexts apply.
element.requirements: Assist in searching for appropriate content.

resource.name: Questionnaire.jurisdiction
resource.title: Questionnaire.jurisdiction
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: A legal or geographic region in which the questionnaire is intended to be used.
element.comment: It may be possible for the questionnaire to be used in jurisdictions other than those for which it was originally designed or intended.

binding.description: Countries and regions within which this artifact is targeted for use.

resource.name: Questionnaire.purpose
resource.title: Questionnaire.purpose
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: Explanation of why this questionnaire is needed and why it has been designed as it has.
element.comment: This element does not describe the usage of the questionnaire. Instead, it provides traceability of ''why'' the resource is either needed or ''why'' it is defined as it is.  This may be used to point to source materials or specifications that drove the structure of this questionnaire.

resource.name: Questionnaire.copyright
resource.title: Questionnaire.copyright
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: A copyright statement relating to the questionnaire and/or its contents. Copyright statements are generally legal restrictions on the use and publishing of the questionnaire.
element.requirements: Consumers must be able to determine any legal restrictions on the use of the questionnaire and/or its content.

resource.name: Questionnaire.approvalDate
resource.title: Questionnaire.approvalDate
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: When the questionnaire was approved by publisher
element.definition: The date on which the resource content was approved by the publisher. Approval happens once when the content is officially approved for usage.
element.comment: The 'date' element may be more recent than the approval date because of minor changes or editorial corrections.

resource.name: Questionnaire.lastReviewDate
resource.title: Questionnaire.lastReviewDate
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: When the questionnaire was last reviewed
element.definition: The date on which the resource content was last reviewed. Review happens periodically after approval but does not change the original approval date.
element.comment: If specified, this date follows the original approval date.
element.requirements: Gives a sense of how "current" the content is.  Resources that have not been reviewed in a long time may have a risk of being less appropriate/relevant.

resource.name: Questionnaire.effectivePeriod
resource.title: Questionnaire.effectivePeriod
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: When the questionnaire is expected to be used
element.definition: The period during which the questionnaire content was or is planned to be in active use.
element.comment: The effective period for a questionnaire  determines when the content is applicable for usage and is independent of publication and review dates. For example, a measure intended to be used for the year 2016 might be published in 2015.
element.requirements: Allows establishing a transition before a resource comes into effect and also allows for a sunsetting  process when new versions of the questionnaire are or are expected to be used instead.

resource.title: Questionnaire.code

element.definition: An identifier for this question or group of questions in a particular terminology such as LOINC.
element.requirements: Allows linking of the complete Questionnaire resources to formal terminologies.  It's common for "panels" of questions to be identified by a code.

binding.description: Codes for questionnaires, groups and individual questions.

resource.title: Questionnaire.item.linkId
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: Unique id for item in questionnaire
element.definition: An identifier that is unique within the Questionnaire allowing linkage to the equivalent item in a QuestionnaireResponse resource.
element.comment: This ''can'' be a meaningful identifier (e.g. a LOINC code) but is not intended to have any meaning.  GUIDs or sequential numbers are appropriate here.
element.requirements: [QuestionnaireResponse](questionnaireresponse.html#) does not require omitted items to be included and may have some items that repeat, so linkage based on position alone is not sufficient.

resource.name: Questionnaire.item.definition
resource.title: Questionnaire.item.definition
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition:
This element is a URI that refers to an [ElementDefinition](elementdefinition.html) that provides information about this item, including information that might otherwise be included in the instance of the Questionnaire resource. A detailed description of the construction of the URI is shown in Comments, below. If this element is present then the following element values MAY be derived from the Element Definition if the corresponding elements of this Questionnaire resource instance have no value:

* code (ElementDefinition.code) 
* type (ElementDefinition.type) 
* required (ElementDefinition.min) 
* repeats (ElementDefinition.max) 
* maxLength (ElementDefinition.maxLength) 
* answerValueSet (ElementDefinition.binding)
* options (ElementDefinition.binding).
element.comment: The uri refers to an ElementDefinition in a [StructureDefinition](structuredefinition.html#) and always starts with the [canonical URL](references.html#canonical) for the target resource. When referring to a StructureDefinition, a fragment identifier is used to specify the element definition by its id [Element.id](element-definitions.html#Element.id). E.g. http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/Observation#Observation.value[x]. In the absence of a fragment identifier, the first/root element definition in the target is the matching element definition.
element.requirements: A common pattern is to define a set of data elements and then build multiple questionnaires for different circumstances to gather the data. This element provides traceability to the common definition and allows the content for the question to come from the underlying definition.

resource.name: Questionnaire.item.code
resource.title: Questionnaire.item.code
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: Corresponding concept for this item in a terminology
element.definition: A terminology code that corresponds to this group or question (e.g. a code from LOINC, which defines many questions and answers).
element.comment: The value may come from the ElementDefinition referred to by .definition.
element.requirements: Allows linking of groups of questions to formal terminologies.

binding.description: Codes for questionnaires, groups and individual questions.

resource.name: Questionnaire.item.prefix
resource.title: Questionnaire.item.prefix
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: A short label for a particular group, question or set of display text within the questionnaire used for reference by the individual completing the questionnaire.
element.comment: These are generally unique within a questionnaire, though this is not guaranteed. Some questionnaires may have multiple questions with the same label with logic to control which gets exposed.  Typically, these won't be used for "display" items, though such use is not prohibited.  Systems SHOULD NOT generate their own prefixes if prefixes are defined for any items within a Questionnaire.
element.requirements: Separating the label from the question text allows improved rendering.  Also, instructions will often refer to specific prefixes, so there's a need for the questionnaire design to have control over what labels are used.

resource.name: Questionnaire.item.text
resource.title: Questionnaire.item.text
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: The name of a section, the text of a question or text content for a display item.
element.comment: When using this element to represent the name of a section, use group type item and also make sure to limit the text element to a short string suitable for display as a section heading.  Group item instructions should be included as a display type item within the group.

resource.name: Questionnaire.item.type
resource.title: Questionnaire.item.type
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: group | display | boolean | decimal | integer | date | dateTime +
element.definition: The type of questionnaire item this is - whether text for display, a grouping of other items or a particular type of data to be captured (string, integer, coded choice, etc.).
element.comment: Additional constraints on the type of answer can be conveyed by extensions. The value may come from the ElementDefinition referred to by .definition.
element.requirements: Defines the format in which the user is to be prompted for the answer.

binding.description: Distinguishes groups from questions and display text and indicates data type for questions.

mapping.map: N/A - MIF rather than RIM level

resource.name: Questionnaire.item.required
resource.title: Questionnaire.item.required
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: Whether the item must be included in data results
element.definition: An indication, if true, that the item must be present in a "completed" QuestionnaireResponse.  If false, the item may be skipped when answering the questionnaire.
element.comment: Questionnaire.item.required only has meaning for elements that are conditionally enabled with enableWhen if the condition evaluates to true.  If an item that contains other items is marked as required, that does not automatically make the contained elements required (though required groups must contain at least one child element). The value may come from the ElementDefinition referred to by .definition.
element.meaningWhenMissing: Items are generally assumed not to be required unless explicitly specified. Systems SHOULD always populate this value

mapping.map: N/A - MIF rather than RIM level

resource.name: Questionnaire.item.repeats
resource.title: Questionnaire.item.repeats
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: An indication, if true, that the item may occur multiple times in the response, collecting multiple answers for questions or multiple sets of answers for groups.
element.comment:
If a question is marked as repeats=true, then multiple answers can be provided for the question in the corresponding QuestionnaireResponse.  When rendering the questionnaire, it is up to the rendering software whether to render the question text for each answer repetition (i.e. "repeat the question") or to simply allow entry/selection of multiple answers for the question (repeat the answers).  Which is most appropriate visually may depend on the type of answer as well as whether there are nested items.

The resulting QuestionnaireResponse will be populated the same way regardless of rendering - one 'question' item with multiple answer values.

 The value may come from the ElementDefinition referred to by .definition.
element.requirements: Items may be used to create set of (related) questions that can be repeated to give multiple answers to such a set.
element.meaningWhenMissing: Items are generally assumed not to repeat unless explicitly specified. Systems SHOULD always populate this value

mapping.map: N/A - MIF rather than RIM level

resource.title: Questionnaire.item.readOnly

element.comment: The value of readOnly elements can be established by asserting  extensions for defaultValues, linkages that support pre-population and/or extensions that support calculation based on other answers.
element.requirements: Allows certain information to be phrased (and rendered) as a question and an answer, while keeping users from changing it.  May also be useful for preventing changes to pre-populated portions of a questionnaire, for calculated values, etc.

resource.name: QuestionnaireResponse.basedOn
resource.title: QuestionnaireResponse.basedOn
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: The order, proposal or plan that is fulfilled in whole or in part by this QuestionnaireResponse.  For example, a ServiceRequest seeking an intake assessment or a decision support recommendation to assess for post-partum depression.
element.requirements: Supports traceability of responsibility for the action and allows linkage of an action to the recommendations acted upon.

resource.name: QuestionnaireResponse.partOf
resource.title: QuestionnaireResponse.partOf
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: A procedure or observation that this questionnaire was performed as part of the execution of.  For example, the surgery a checklist was executed as part of.
element.comment: Composition of questionnaire responses will be handled by the parent questionnaire having answers that reference the child questionnaire.  For relationships to referrals, and other types of requests, use basedOn.

resource.name: QuestionnaireResponse.questionnaire
resource.title: QuestionnaireResponse.questionnaire
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: The Questionnaire that defines and organizes the questions for which answers are being provided.
element.comment: If a QuestionnaireResponse references a Questionnaire, then the QuestionnaireResponse structure must be consistent with the Questionnaire (i.e. questions must be organized into the same groups, nested questions must still be nested, etc.).
element.requirements: Needed to allow editing of the questionnaire response in a manner that enforces the constraints of the original form.

resource.name: QuestionnaireResponse.status
resource.title: QuestionnaireResponse.status
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: The position of the questionnaire response within its overall lifecycle.
element.comment: This element is labeled as a modifier because the status contains codes that mark the resource as not currently valid.
element.requirements: The information on Questionnaire resources  may possibly be gathered during multiple sessions and altered after considered being finished.
element.isModifierReason: This element is labelled as a modifier because it is a status element that contains status entered-in-error which means that the resource should not be treated as valid

binding.description: Lifecycle status of the questionnaire response.

mapping.map: .statusCode (also whether there's a revisionControlAct - and possibly mood to distinguish "in-progress" from "published)

resource.name: QuestionnaireResponse.subject
resource.title: QuestionnaireResponse.subject
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: The subject of the questionnaire response.  This could be a patient, organization, practitioner, device, etc.  This is who/what the answers apply to, but is not necessarily the source of information.
element.comment: If the Questionnaire declared a subjectType, the resource pointed to by this element must be an instance of one of the listed types.
element.requirements: Allows linking the answers to the individual the answers describe.  May also affect access control.

resource.name: QuestionnaireResponse.encounter
resource.title: QuestionnaireResponse.encounter
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: The Encounter during which this questionnaire response was created or to which the creation of this record is tightly associated.
element.comment: This will typically be the encounter the event occurred within, but some activities may be initiated prior to or after the official completion of an encounter but still be tied to the context of the encounter. A questionnaire that was initiated during an encounter but not fully completed during the encounter would still generally be associated with the encounter.
element.requirements: Provides context for the information that was captured.  May also affect access control.

resource.name: QuestionnaireResponse.authored
resource.title: QuestionnaireResponse.authored
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: The date and/or time that this set of answers were last changed.
element.comment:
May be different from the lastUpdateTime of the resource itself, because that reflects when the data was known to the server, not when the data was captured.

This element is optional to allow for systems that might not know the value, however it SHOULD be populated if possible.
element.requirements: Clinicians need to be able to check the date that the information in the questionnaire was collected, to derive the context of the answers.

resource.name: QuestionnaireResponse.author
resource.title: QuestionnaireResponse.author
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: Person who received and recorded the answers
element.definition: Person who received the answers to the questions in the QuestionnaireResponse and recorded them in the system.
element.comment: Mapping a subject's answers to multiple choice options and determining what to put in the textual answer is a matter of interpretation.  Authoring by device would indicate that some portion of the questionnaire had been auto-populated.
element.requirements: Need to know who interpreted the subject's answers to the questions in the questionnaire, and selected the appropriate options for answers.

resource.name: QuestionnaireResponse.source
resource.title: QuestionnaireResponse.source
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: The person who answered the questions
element.definition: The person who answered the questions about the subject.
element.comment: If not specified, no inference can be made about who provided the data.
element.requirements: When answering questions about a subject that is minor, incapable of answering or an animal, another human source may answer the questions.

element.short: Canonical identifier for this risk evidence synthesis, represented as a URI (globally unique)

In some cases, the resource can no longer be found at the stated url, but the url itself cannot change. Implementations can use the [meta.source](resource.html#meta) element to indicate where the current master source of the resource can be found.

resource.name: ServiceRequest.identifier
resource.title: ServiceRequest.identifier
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: Identifiers assigned to this order instance by the orderer and/or the receiver and/or order fulfiller.
element.comment: The identifier.type element is used to distinguish between the identifiers assigned by the orderer (known as the 'Placer' in HL7 v2) and the producer of the observations in response to the order (known as the 'Filler' in HL7 v2).  For further discussion and examples see the resource notes section below.

resource.name: ServiceRequest.instantiatesCanonical
resource.title: ServiceRequest.instantiatesCanonical
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: The URL pointing to a FHIR-defined protocol, guideline, orderset or other definition that is adhered to in whole or in part by this ServiceRequest.
element.comment: Note: This is a business identifier, not a resource identifier (see [discussion](resource.html#identifiers)).  It is best practice for the identifier to only appear on a single resource instance, however business practices may occasionally dictate that multiple resource instances with the same identifier can exist - possibly even with different resource types.  For example, multiple Patient and a Person resource instance might share the same social insurance number.

resource.name: ServiceRequest.instantiatesUri
resource.title: ServiceRequest.instantiatesUri
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: The URL pointing to an externally maintained protocol, guideline, orderset or other definition that is adhered to in whole or in part by this ServiceRequest.
element.comment: This might be an HTML page, PDF, etc. or could just be a non-resolvable URI identifier.

resource.name: ServiceRequest.basedOn
resource.title: ServiceRequest.basedOn
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: Plan/proposal/order fulfilled by this request.

resource.name: ServiceRequest.replaces
resource.title: ServiceRequest.replaces
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: The request takes the place of the referenced completed or terminated request(s).

mapping.map: Handled by message location of ORC (ORC.1=RO or RU)

resource.name: ServiceRequest.requisition
resource.title: ServiceRequest.requisition
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: A shared identifier common to all service requests that were authorized more or less simultaneously by a single author, representing the composite or group identifier.
element.comment: Requests are linked either by a "basedOn" relationship (i.e. one request is fulfilling another) or by having a common requisition. Requests that are part of the same requisition are generally treated independently from the perspective of changing their state or maintaining them after initial creation.
element.requirements: Some business processes need to know if multiple items were ordered as part of the same "requisition" for billing or other purposes.

resource.name: ServiceRequest.status
resource.title: ServiceRequest.status
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: draft | active | on-hold | revoked | completed | entered-in-error | unknown
element.definition: The status of the order.
element.comment: The status is generally fully in the control of the requester - they determine whether the order is draft or active and, after it has been activated, competed, cancelled or suspended. States relating to the activities of the performer are reflected on either the corresponding event (see [Event Pattern](event.html) for general discussion) or using the [Task](task.html) resource.
element.isModifierReason: This element is labeled as a modifier because it is a status element that contains status entered-in-error which means that the resource should not be treated as valid

binding.description: The status of a service order.

resource.name: ServiceRequest.intent
resource.title: ServiceRequest.intent
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: proposal | plan | directive | order | original-order | reflex-order | filler-order | instance-order | option
element.definition: Whether the request is a proposal, plan, an original order or a reflex order.
element.comment: This element is labeled as a modifier because the intent alters when and how the resource is actually applicable.
element.isModifierReason: This element changes the interpretation of all descriptive attributes. For example "the time the request is recommended to occur" vs. "the time the request is authorized to occur" or "who is recommended to perform the request" vs. "who is authorized to perform the request

binding.description: The kind of service request.

mapping.map: .moodCode (nuances beyond PRP/PLAN/RQO would need to be elsewhere)

resource.name: ServiceRequest.category
resource.title: ServiceRequest.category
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: A code that classifies the service for searching, sorting and display purposes (e.g. "Surgical Procedure").
element.comment: There may be multiple axis of categorization depending on the context or use case for retrieving or displaying the resource.  The level of granularity is defined by the category concepts in the value set.
element.requirements: Used for filtering what service request are retrieved and displayed.

binding.description: Classification of the requested service.

resource.name: ServiceRequest.priority
resource.title: ServiceRequest.priority
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: Indicates how quickly the ServiceRequest should be addressed with respect to other requests.
element.meaningWhenMissing: If missing, this task should be performed with normal priority

binding.description: Identifies the level of importance to be assigned to actioning the request.

resource.name: ServiceRequest.doNotPerform
resource.title: ServiceRequest.doNotPerform
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: True if service/procedure should not be performed
element.definition: Set this to true if the record is saying that the service/procedure should NOT be performed.
element.comment: In general, only the code and timeframe will be present, though occasional additional qualifiers such as body site or even performer could be included to narrow the scope of the prohibition.  If the ServiceRequest.code and ServiceRequest.doNotPerform both contain negation, that will reinforce prohibition and should not have a double negative interpretation.
element.requirements: Used for do not ambulate, do not elevate head of bed, do not flush NG tube, do not take blood pressure on a certain arm, etc.
element.meaningWhenMissing: If missing, the request is a positive request e.g. "do perform"
element.isModifierReason: If true this element negates the specified action. For Example,  instead of a request for a procedure, it is a request for the procedure to not occur.

resource.name: ServiceRequest.code
resource.title: ServiceRequest.code
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: A code that identifies a particular service (i.e., procedure, diagnostic investigation, or panel of investigations) that have been requested.
element.comment: Many laboratory and radiology procedure codes embed the specimen/organ system in the test order name, for example,  serum or serum/plasma glucose, or a chest x-ray. The specimen might not be recorded separately from the test code.

binding.description: Codes for tests or services that can be carried out by a designated individual, organization or healthcare service.  For laboratory, LOINC is  (preferred)[http://build.fhir.org/terminologies.html#preferred] and a valueset using LOINC Order codes is available [here](valueset-diagnostic-requests.html).

resource.name: ServiceRequest.orderDetail
resource.title: ServiceRequest.orderDetail
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: Additional details and instructions about the how the services are to be delivered.   For example, and order for a urinary catheter may have an order detail for an external or indwelling catheter, or an order for a bandage may require additional instructions specifying how the bandage should be applied.
element.comment: For information from the medical record intended to support the delivery of the requested services, use the `supportingInformation` element.

binding.description: Codified order entry details which are based on order context.

resource.name: ServiceRequest.quantity[x]
resource.title: ServiceRequest.quantity[x]
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: An amount of service being requested which can be a quantity ( for example $1,500 home modification), a ratio ( for example, 20 half day visits per month), or a range (2.0 to 1.8 Gy per fraction).
element.requirements: When ordering a service the number of service items may need to be specified separately from the the service item.

resource.name: ServiceRequest.subject
resource.title: ServiceRequest.subject
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: Individual or Entity the service is ordered for
element.definition: On whom or what the service is to be performed. This is usually a human patient, but can also be requested on animals, groups of humans or animals, devices such as dialysis machines, or even locations (typically for environmental scans).

resource.name: ServiceRequest.encounter
resource.title: ServiceRequest.encounter
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: Encounter in which the request was created
element.definition: An encounter that provides additional information about the healthcare context in which this request is made.

resource.name: ServiceRequest.occurrence[x]
resource.title: ServiceRequest.occurrence[x]
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: The date/time at which the requested service should occur.

resource.name: ServiceRequest.asNeeded[x]
resource.title: ServiceRequest.asNeeded[x]
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: If a CodeableConcept is present, it indicates the pre-condition for performing the service.  For example "pain", "on flare-up", etc.

binding.description: A coded concept identifying the pre-condition that should hold prior to performing a procedure.  For example "pain", "on flare-up", etc.

mapping.map: boolean: precondition.negationInd (inversed - so negationInd = true means asNeeded=false CodeableConcept: precondition.observationEventCriterion[code="Assertion"].value

resource.name: ServiceRequest.authoredOn
resource.title: ServiceRequest.authoredOn
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: When the request transitioned to being actionable.

resource.name: ServiceRequest.requester
resource.title: ServiceRequest.requester
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: The individual who initiated the request and has responsibility for its activation.
element.comment: This not the dispatcher, but rather who is the authorizer.  This element is not intended to handle delegation which would generally be managed through the Provenance resource.

resource.name: ServiceRequest.performerType
resource.title: ServiceRequest.performerType
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: Desired type of performer for doing the requested service.
element.comment: This is a  role, not  a participation type.  In other words, does not describe the task but describes the capacity.  For example, “compounding pharmacy”, “psychiatrist” or “internal referral”.

binding.description: Indicates specific responsibility of an individual within the care team, such as "Primary physician", "Team coordinator", "Caregiver", etc.

resource.name: ServiceRequest.performer
resource.title: ServiceRequest.performer
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: The desired performer for doing the requested service.  For example, the surgeon, dermatopathologist, endoscopist, etc.
element.comment: If multiple performers are present, it is interpreted as a list of *alternative* performers without any preference regardless of order.  If order of preference is needed use the [request-performerOrder extension](extension-request-performerorder.html).  Use CareTeam to represent a group of performers (for example, Practitioner A *and* Practitioner B).

mapping.map: PRT, Practitioner: PRD-2/PRD-7 where PRD-3 = RT; Organization: PRD-10 where PRD-3 = RT

resource.name: ServiceRequest.locationCode
resource.title: ServiceRequest.locationCode
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: The preferred location(s) where the procedure should actually happen in coded or free text form. E.g. at home or nursing day care center.

binding.description: A location type where services are delivered.

resource.name: ServiceRequest.locationReference
resource.title: ServiceRequest.locationReference
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: A reference to the the preferred location(s) where the procedure should actually happen. E.g. at home or nursing day care center.

resource.name: ServiceRequest.reasonCode
resource.title: ServiceRequest.reasonCode
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: An explanation or justification for why this service is being requested in coded or textual form.   This is often for billing purposes.  May relate to the resources referred to in `supportingInfo`.
element.comment: This element represents why the referral is being made and may be used to decide how the service will be performed, or even if it will be performed at all.   Use `CodeableConcept.text` element if the data is free (uncoded) text as shown in the [CT Scan example](servicerequest-example-di.html).

binding.description: Diagnosis or problem codes justifying the reason for requesting the service investigation.

resource.name: ServiceRequest.reasonReference
resource.title: ServiceRequest.reasonReference
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: Indicates another resource that provides a justification for why this service is being requested.   May relate to the resources referred to in `supportingInfo`.
element.comment: This element represents why the referral is being made and may be used to decide how the service will be performed, or even if it will be performed at all.    To be as specific as possible,  a reference to  *Observation* or *Condition* should be used if available.  Otherwise when referencing  *DiagnosticReport*  it should contain a finding  in `DiagnosticReport.conclusion` and/or `DiagnosticReport.conclusionCode`.   When using a reference to *DocumentReference*, the target document should contain clear findings language providing the relevant reason for this service request.  Use  the CodeableConcept text element in `ServiceRequest.reasonCode` if the data is free (uncoded) text as shown in the [CT Scan example](servicerequest-example-di.html).

resource.name: ServiceRequest.insurance
resource.title: ServiceRequest.insurance
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: Insurance plans, coverage extensions, pre-authorizations and/or pre-determinations that may be needed for delivering the requested service.

resource.name: ServiceRequest.supportingInfo
resource.title: ServiceRequest.supportingInfo
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: Additional clinical information about the patient or specimen that may influence the services or their interpretations.     This information includes diagnosis, clinical findings and other observations.  In laboratory ordering these are typically referred to as "ask at order entry questions (AOEs)".  This includes observations explicitly requested by the producer (filler) to provide context or supporting information needed to complete the order. For example,  reporting the amount of inspired oxygen for blood gas measurements.
element.comment: To represent information about how the services are to be delivered use the `instructions` element.

resource.name: ServiceRequest.specimen
resource.title: ServiceRequest.specimen
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: One or more specimens that the laboratory procedure will use.
element.comment: Many diagnostic procedures need a specimen, but the request itself is not actually about the specimen. This element is for when the diagnostic is requested on already existing specimens and the request points to the specimen it applies to.    Conversely, if the request is entered first with an unknown specimen, then the [Specimen](specimen.html) resource points to the ServiceRequest.

resource.name: ServiceRequest.bodySite
resource.title: ServiceRequest.bodySite
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: Anatomic location where the procedure should be performed. This is the target site.
element.comment: Only used if not implicit in the code found in ServiceRequest.code.  If the use case requires BodySite to be handled as a separate resource instead of an inline coded element (e.g. to identify and track separately)  then use the standard extension [procedure-targetBodyStructure](extension-procedure-targetbodystructure.html).
element.requirements: Knowing where the procedure is performed is important for tracking if multiple sites are possible.

binding.description: Codes describing anatomical locations. May include laterality.

resource.name: ServiceRequest.note

resource.name: ServiceRequest.patientInstruction
resource.title: ServiceRequest.patientInstruction

resource.name: ServiceRequest.relevantHistory
resource.title: ServiceRequest.relevantHistory

element.definition: Key events in the history of the request.
element.comment: This might not include provenances for all versions of the request – only those deemed “relevant” or important.This SHALL NOT include the Provenance associated with this current version of the resource.  (If that provenance is deemed to be a “relevant” change, it will need to be added as part of a later update.  Until then, it can be queried directly as the Provenance that points to this version using _revincludeAll Provenances should have some historical version of this Request as their subject.

element.comment: Asserting this rule set restricts the content to be only understood by a limited set of trading partners. This inherently limits the usefulness of the data in the long term. element.comment: Language is provided to support indexing and accessibility (typically, services such as text to speech use the language tag). The html language tag in the narrative applies  to the narrative. The language tag on the resource may be used to specify the language of other presentations generated from the data in the resource. Not all the content has to be in the base language. The Resource.language should not be assumed to apply to the narrative automatically. If a language is specified, it should it also be specified on the div element in the html (see rules in HTML5 for information about the relationship between xml:lang and the html lang attribute).

element.short: Text summary of the resource, for human interpretation
element.definition: A human-readable narrative that contains a summary of the resource and can be used to represent the content of the resource to a human. The narrative need not encode all the structured data, but is required to contain sufficient detail to make it "clinically safe" for a human to just read the narrative. Resource definitions may define what content should be represented in the narrative to ensure clinical safety.
element.comment: Contained resources do not have narrative. Resources that are not contained SHOULD have a narrative. In some cases, a resource may only have text with little or no additional discrete data (as long as all minOccurs=1 elements are satisfied).  This may be necessary for data from legacy systems where information is captured as a "text blob" or where text is additionally entered raw or narrated and encoded information is added later.

resource.name: StructureDefinition.type
resource.title: StructureDefinition.type

element.short: Type defined or constrained by this structure
element.definition: The type this structure describes. If the derivation kind is 'specialization' then this is the master definition for a type, and there is always one of these (a data type, an extension, a resource, including abstract ones). Otherwise the structure definition is a constraint on the stated type (and in this case, the type cannot be an abstract type).  References are URLs that are relative to http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition e.g. "string" is a reference to http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/string. Absolute URLs are only allowed in logical models.
element.comment:
Note that in the case of constraints, the type could be determined by chasing through the baseDefinition references until a concrete structure (derivation = specialization) is reached, or by looking at the path of the first element in the snapshot - if present - but providing the type directly makes for simpler tooling and indexing. 

The type must match the elements defined in the differential and the snapshot. For all FHIR defined types, the path name of the element will start with the type name. For logical models, where the type is a URL, the type name SHOULD start with the tail of the type URL where required.

binding.description: Either a resource or a data type, including logical model types.

The FHIR Project provides a number of tools/services to populate snapshots from differential constraints. Logical Models have a base of "Element" or another logical model.

This may be necessary for data from legacy systems where information is captured as a "text blob" or where text is additionally entered raw or narrated and encoded information is added later.

resource.title: StructureMap.url

element.short: Canonical identifier for this structure map, represented as a URI (globally unique)
element.definition: An absolute URI that is used to identify this structure map when it is referenced in a specification, model, design or an instance; also called its canonical identifier. This SHOULD be globally unique and SHOULD be a literal address at which at which an authoritative instance of this structure map is (or will be) published. This URL can be the target of a canonical reference. It SHALL remain the same when the structure map is stored on different servers.
element.comment:
Can be a urn:uuid: or a urn:oid: but real http: addresses are preferred.  Multiple instances may share the same URL if they have a distinct version.

The determination of when to create a new version of a resource (same url, new version) vs. defining a new artifact is up to the author.  Considerations for making this decision are found in [Technical and Business Versions](resource.html#versions). 

In some cases, the resource can no longer be found at the stated url, but the url itself cannot change. Implementations can use the [meta.source](resource.html#meta) element to indicate where the current master source of the resource can be found.
element.requirements: Allows the structure map to be referenced by a single globally unique identifier.

Not all the content has to be in the base language. The Resource.language should not be assumed to apply to the narrative automatically. If a language is specified, it should it also be specified on the div element in the html (see rules in HTML5 for information about the relationship between xml:lang and the html lang attribute).

Resource definitions may define what content should be represented in the narrative to ensure clinical safety.
element.comment: Contained resources do not have narrative. Resources that are not contained SHOULD have a narrative. In some cases, a resource may only have text with little or no additional discrete data (as long as all minOccurs=1 elements are satisfied).  This may be necessary for data from legacy systems where information is captured as a "text blob" or where text is additionally entered raw or narrated and encoded information is added later.

resource.name: Task.basedOn
resource.title: Task.basedOn
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: BasedOn refers to a higher-level authorization that triggered the creation of the task.  It references a "request" resource such as a ServiceRequest, MedicationRequest, ServiceRequest, CarePlan, etc. which is distinct from the "request" resource the task is seeking to fulfill.  This latter resource is referenced by FocusOn.  For example, based on a ServiceRequest (= BasedOn), a task is created to fulfill a procedureRequest ( = FocusOn ) to collect a specimen from a patient.

resource.name: Task.groupIdentifier
resource.title: Task.groupIdentifier
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: An identifier that links together multiple tasks and other requests that were created in the same context.
element.requirements: Billing and/or reporting can be linked to whether multiple requests were created as a single unit.

resource.name: Task.partOf
resource.title: Task.partOf
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: Task that this particular task is part of.
element.comment: This should usually be 0..1.
element.requirements: Allows tasks to be broken down into sub-steps (and this division can occur independent of the original task).

resource.name: Task.status
resource.title: Task.status
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: The current status of the task.
element.requirements: These states enable coordination of task status with off-the-shelf workflow solutions that support automation of tasks.
element.isModifierReason: This element is labeled as a modifier because it is a status element that contains status entered-in-error which means that the resource should not be treated as valid

binding.description: The current status of the task.

resource.name: Task.statusReason
resource.title: Task.statusReason

element.comment: This applies to the current status.  Look at the history of the task to see reasons for past statuses.

binding.description: Codes to identify the reason for current status.  These will typically be specific to a particular workflow.

resource.name: Task.businessStatus
resource.title: Task.businessStatus
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.definition: Contains business-specific nuances of the business state.
element.requirements: There's often a need to track substates of a task - this is often variable by specific workflow implementation.

binding.description: The domain-specific business-contextual sub-state of the task.  For example: "Blood drawn", "IV inserted", "Awaiting physician signature", etc.

resource.name: Task.intent
resource.title: Task.intent
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: unknown | proposal | plan | order | original-order | reflex-order | filler-order | instance-order | option
element.definition: Indicates the "level" of actionability associated with the Task, i.e. i+R[9]Cs this a proposed task, a planned task, an actionable task, etc.
element.comment:
This element is immutable.  Proposed tasks, planned tasks, etc. must be distinct instances.

In most cases, Tasks will have an intent of "order".

binding.description: Distinguishes whether the task is a proposal, plan or full order.

resource.name: Task.priority
resource.title: Task.priority

element.requirements: Used to identify the service level expected while performing a task.
element.meaningWhenMissing: If missing, this task should be performed with normal priority

binding.description: The task's priority.

resource.name: Task.code
resource.title: Task.code

element.requirements: For some tasks it may be important to know the link between the encounter the task originated within.

resource.name: Task.executionPeriod

resource.name: Task.authoredOn
resource.title: Task.authoredOn

resource.name: Task.lastModified

resource.name: Task.performerType

element.short: Text summary of the resource, for human interpretation
element.definition: A human-readable narrative that contains a summary of the resource and can be used to represent the content of the resource to a human. The narrative need not encode all the structured data, but is required to contain sufficient detail to make it "clinically safe" for a human to just read the narrative. Resource definitions may define what content should be represented in the narrative to ensure clinical safety.
element.comment: Contained resources do not have narrative. Resources that are not contained SHOULD have a narrative. In some cases, a resource may only have text with little or no additional discrete data (as long as all minOccurs=1 elements are satisfied).  This may be necessary for data from legacy systems where information is captured as a "text blob" or where text is additionally entered raw or narrated and encoded information is added later.

resource.name: TestScript.url
resource.title: TestScript.url

element.short: Canonical identifier for this test script, represented as a URI (globally unique)
element.definition: An absolute URI that is used to identify this test script when it is referenced in a specification, model, design or an instance; also called its canonical identifier. This SHOULD be globally unique and SHOULD be a literal address at which at which an authoritative instance of this test script is (or will be) published. This URL can be the target of a canonical reference. It SHALL remain the same when the test script is stored on different servers.
element.comment:
Can be a urn:uuid: or a urn:oid: but real http: addresses are preferred.  Multiple instances may share the same URL if they have a distinct version.

The determination of when to create a new version of a resource (same url, new version) vs. defining a new artifact is up to the author.  Considerations for making this decision are found in [Technical and Business Versions](resource.html#versions). 

In some cases, the resource can no longer be found at the stated url, but the url itself cannot change. Implementations can use the [meta.source](resource.html#meta) element to indicate where the current master source of the resource can be found.
element.requirements: Allows the test script to be referenced by a single globally unique identifier.

resource.title: TestScript.identifier

element.short: Additional identifier for the test script
element.definition: A formal identifier that is used to identify this test script when it is represented in other formats, or referenced in a specification, model, design or an instance.
element.comment: Typically, this is used for identifiers that can go in an HL7 V3 II (instance identifier) data type, and can then identify this test script outside of FHIR, where it is not possible to use the logical URI.
element.requirements: Allows externally provided and/or usable business identifiers to be easily associated with the module.

resource.name: TestScript.version
resource.title: TestScript.version
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: Business version of the test script
element.definition: The identifier that is used to identify this version of the test script when it is referenced in a specification, model, design or instance. This is an arbitrary value managed by the test script author and is not expected to be globally unique. For example, it might be a timestamp (e.g. yyyymmdd) if a managed version is not available. There is also no expectation that versions can be placed in a lexicographical sequence.
element.comment: There may be different test script instances that have the same identifier but different versions.  The version can be appended to the url in a reference to allow a reference to a particular business version of the test script with the format [url]|[version].

resource.title: TestScript.date

element.definition: The date  (and optionally time) when the test script was published. The date must change when the business version changes and it must change if the status code changes. In addition, it should change when the substantive content of the test script changes.
element.comment: Note that this is not the same as the resource last-modified-date, since the resource may be a secondary representation of the test script. Additional specific dates may be added as extensions or be found by consulting Provenances associated with past versions of the resource.

resource.name: TestScript.publisher
resource.title: TestScript.publisher
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: Name of the publisher (organization or individual)
element.definition: The name of the organization or individual that published the test script.
element.comment: Usually an organization but may be an individual. The publisher (or steward) of the test script is the organization or individual primarily responsible for the maintenance and upkeep of the test script. This is not necessarily the same individual or organization that developed and initially authored the content. The publisher is the primary point of contact for questions or issues with the test script. This item SHOULD be populated unless the information is available from context.
element.requirements: Helps establish the "authority/credibility" of the test script.  May also allow for contact.

resource.title: TestScript.contact

resource.name: TestScript.description
resource.title: TestScript.description
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: Natural language description of the test script
element.definition: A free text natural language description of the test script from a consumer's perspective.
element.comment: This description can be used to capture details such as why the test script was built, comments about misuse, instructions for clinical use and interpretation, literature references, examples from the paper world, etc. It is not a rendering of the test script as conveyed in the 'text' field of the resource itself. This item SHOULD be populated unless the information is available from context (e.g. the language of the test script is presumed to be the predominant language in the place the test script was created).

resource.title: TestScript.useContext

element.short: The context that the content is intended to support
element.definition: The content was developed with a focus and intent of supporting the contexts that are listed. element.comment: When multiple useContexts are specified, there is no expectation that all or any of the contexts apply.
element.requirements: Assist in searching for appropriate content.

element.short: Canonical identifier for this value set, represented as a URI (globally unique)
element.definition: An absolute URI that is used to identify this value set when it is referenced in a specification, model, design or an instance; also called its canonical identifier. resource.title: ValueSet.description

element.short: Natural language description of the value set
element.definition: A free text natural language description of the value set from a consumer's perspective. The textual description specifies the span of meanings for concepts to be included within the Value Set Expansion, and also may specify the intended use and limitations of the Value Set.
element.comment: This description can be used to capture details such as why the value set was built, comments about misuse, instructions for clinical use and interpretation, literature references, examples from the paper world, etc. It is not a rendering of the value set as conveyed in the 'text' field of the resource itself. This item SHOULD be populated unless the information is available from context (e.g. the language of the value set is presumed to be the predominant language in the place the value set was created).The description is not intended to describe the semantics of the Value Set - there are no intrinsic semantics separate from the codes contained in its expansion. The description should capture its intended use, which is needed for ensuring integrity for its use in models across future changes. A description should be provided unless the value set is a contained resource (e.g. an anonymous value set in a profile). Most registries will require a description.

resource.name: ValueSet.immutable
resource.title: ValueSet.immutable
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: Indicates whether or not any change to the content logical definition may occur
element.definition: If this is set to 'true', then no new versions of the content logical definition can be created.  Note: Other metadata might still change.
element.comment: Normally immutability is set to 'false', which is the default assumption if it is not populated.  Note that the implication is that if this is set to 'true', there may be only one ValueSet version for this definition. Immutability tends to be set to 'true' in one of two cases: - Where the value set, by the nature of its usage, cannot change.  For example "All specializations of ACT in ActClassCode" - Where there's no safe way to express the "Purpose" such that someone else could safely make changes to the value set definition. Source workflow control must guarantee that the same URI always yields the same definition.

element.short: Fixed date for references with no specified version (transitive)
element.definition: The Locked Date is  the effective date that is used to determine the version of all referenced Code Systems and Value Set Definitions included in the compose that are not already tied to a specific version.
element.comment: With a defined lockedDate the value set is considered "Locked". Otherwise, the value set may have different expansions as underlying code systems and/or value sets evolve. If a value set specifies a version for include and exclude statements, and also specifies a locked date, the specified versions need to be available that date, or the value set will not be usable.

resource.name: ValueSet.compose.inactive
resource.title: ValueSet.compose.inactive
resource.purpose: Data Elements are defined for each element to assist in questionnaire construction etc

element.short: Whether inactive codes are in the value set
element.definition: Whether inactive codes - codes that are not approved for current use - are in the value set. If inactive = true, inactive codes are to be included in the expansion, if inactive = false, the inactive codes will not be included in the expansion. If absent, the behavior is determined by the implementation, or by the applicable $expand parameters (but generally, inactive codes would be expected to be included).
element.comment:
Note that in the FHIR terminology framework, "deprecated" does not mean inactive, but in some code systems, e.g. LOINC, "deprecated" does mean inactive. Code systems should define what codes are considered to be inactive. If this is not clearly defined (including in the FHIR code system resource), then all codes are assumed to be active.

The Value Set Definition specification defines an ActiveOnly element, which is the reverse of this element e.g. (ValueSet.compose.inactive=FALSE) is the same as (VSD.ActiveOnly=TRUE).
